channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: The European Parliament Is Drifting Toward Evidence on Nicotine
item.description: The European Parliament’s nicotine debate appears to be moving closer to the evidence. That matters because policy built on fear alone cannot explain why cigarettes, vapes, pouches and heated tobacco should not be treated as the same public health problem. A risk-based approach would still protect young people and regulate products responsibly, but it would also recognise the role safer alternatives can play for adults who smoke. Europe has a chance to make nicotine policy more scientific, more proportionate and more useful. (Published on September 16, 2026byworldvapersalliance.com)

item.title: Europe Is Protecting Cigarettes from Their Competitors
item.description: Europe’s nicotine policy risks protecting cigarettes from competition by making safer alternatives harder to access, afford or communicate clearly. That is a dangerous inversion of public health priorities: the most harmful product remains familiar while lower-risk options face suspicion and restriction. Adult smokers need a market where moving away from combustion is easier than staying with it. Regulation should challenge cigarettes, not shield them from the products that could make them less dominant. (Published on September 17, 2026bysubstack.com)
